assumptions: Source assumption: source and observer move collinearly at constant velocities relative to the same homogeneous acoustic medium; source frequency and medium wave speed constant.
Source assumption: source speed below sound speed for separated wavefronts, excluding shock/sonic-boom regime.
Application profile: observer also subsonic to retain the ordinary positive wave-arrival branch and avoid extrapolating across a wave-catching boundary.
Source scope: classical acoustics, not relativistic electromagnetic waves, and no source/observer crossing within the interval.

gaps: Add source_wave_frequency, observed_wave_frequency, wave_phase_speed and both signed medium-frame endpoint-velocity meanings. Hz and m/s exist; no kHz/MHz factors are inlined. Context must identify a common medium frame, acoustic mode and propagation direction.

models.inverse_notes: For f_s given f_o,v,u_s,u_o: f_s=f_o*(v-u_s)/(v+u_o), require f_o>0,v>0,v+u_o>0 and original subsonic guards; unique. For u_s given f_o,f_s,v,u_o: u_s=v-f_s*(v+u_o)/f_o, require f_o>0,f_s>0 and reconstruction satisfying -v<u_s<v. For u_o given f_o,f_s,v,u_s: u_o=f_o*(v-u_s)/f_s-v, require f_s>0 and reconstructed -v<u_o<v. For v given frequencies and velocities: v=(f_o*u_s+f_s*u_o)/(f_o-f_s), require f_o!=f_s and v>0 larger than both velocity magnitudes (equivalently original four velocity guards). Example f_o=400/3,f_s=100,v=300,u_o=20 -> u_s=60; substituting the two arrival events restores 400/3 Hz. Invert v from that same case -> (8000+2000)/(100/3)=300. If f_o=f_s, u_o=-u_s gives no constraint on admissible v, otherwise no solution; f_o=0 excluded in this positive-frequency branch. In the stationary case u_s=u_o=0, f_o=f_s=150 and shift exactly zero for any admissible supplied v. All mentioned admissible inverses have one root; inversion is algebraic, not causal identification from frequency alone.
limitations: Changing line-of-sight geometry requires updating the kinematic description; it is not covered by simply using total speed.
No energy, amplitude, intensity or perceived loudness/pitch-scale mapping is claimed.
The source's description of applications to light does not justify using this medium-dependent equation for relativistic light Doppler shifts.
Reported textbook results are rounded pedagogical calculations, not experimental calibration or uncertainty estimates.

references.method: Published Example 17.8(a) gives 167 Hz (kept as expected, not replaced by 167.213...). Half the final integer-Hz reporting step is 0.5 Hz; the nominal rounded inputs yield an error about 0.213 Hz.

Published Example 17.8(a) gives 136 Hz after passage; keep this expected rather than recomputing 136 exactly for a different dataset. Nominal source data produce 136 Hz; tolerance 0.5 Hz follows integer reporting.

Limiting identity supported by Example 17.8(b): endpoints with equal laboratory velocity maintain their separation, so arrival intervals equal emission intervals. In this signed convention u_o=-u_s; f_o-f_s=0. A 1e-10 Hz tolerance only covers floating-point evaluation, not measurement precision.

Independent synthetic spacetime construction: source at x=0 moving +60 m/s, observer initially at x=30 m moving -20 m/s; waves travel +300 m/s. First front meets observer at 30/320=0.09375 s. Second emitted at 0.01 s from x=0.6 meets at t=0.10125 s by solving 0.6+300*(t-0.01)=30-20*t. Arrival spacing 0.0075 s yields 133 1/3 Hz. This constructs two events rather than substituting in the serialized frequency expression; tolerance covers repeating decimal arithmetic.
references.provenance: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/17-7-the-doppler-effect# wavefront-emission derivation; independent synthetic endpoint geometry

rejection_cases.reason: At sonic source speed the forward wavefront spacing and denominator vanish; no finite ordinary Doppler frequency.
Observer velocity relative to the medium is not supplied; it must not be silently assumed zero.

relationship.locator: University Physics 1 Eq. 17.20 and Table 17.4; subsonic derivation preceding Eq. 17.18; Example 17.8
relationship.original_equation: f_o = f_s (v +/- v_o)/(v -/+ v_s), top signs for approach
relationship.translation_notes: Introduce signed u_s=+v_s for source motion toward observer and -v_s for recession; u_o=+v_o for observer motion toward source and -v_o for recession. These are independent medium-frame signed velocities, not a single relative speed. Thus source approaching a stationary observer sets u_o=0,u_s>=0. Source subsonic condition becomes -v<u_s<v; application profile imposes -v<u_o<v for the ordinary forward wave-crossing branch as well. Preserve v-u_s>0 denominator guard. Hz*(m/s)/(m/s)=Hz. No constants or frequency-unit scaling appear. This classical acoustic equation is not a light Doppler equation.

sources.evidence: Source and observer motion relative to the medium enter different factors. The derivation uses subsonic source motion and collinear propagation. A 150 Hz horn at 35.0 m/s with sound speed 340 m/s gives reported 167 Hz approaching and 136 Hz receding; comoving endpoints have no shift.

models.summary: Single acoustic Doppler law for subsonic collinear source and observer motion in a homogeneous medium. Includes approaching or receding stationary-observer cases and comoving endpoints without separate model copies.
models.title: Collinear acoustic Doppler frequency in the medium frame

variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure, and constant collinear subsonic endpoint velocities. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s.
variables.definition: Acoustic cycles emitted per unit time by the source under classical common time in the medium frame.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive, constant over the modeled interval.

variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure, and constant collinear subsonic endpoint velocities. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s.
variables.definition: Positive acoustic propagation speed relative to the resting medium for the selected mode and state.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; supplied for medium composition, phase, temperature, pressure and frequency regime; not assumed 340 or 343 m/s.

variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure, and constant collinear subsonic endpoint velocities. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s.
variables.definition: Signed source velocity along the propagation line, relative to the medium, positive toward the observer.
variables.domain: Finite -v<u_s<v. Zero is a stationary source.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced signed u_s maps to +/- source v_s; positive toward observer.

variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure, and constant collinear subsonic endpoint velocities. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s.
variables.definition: Signed observer velocity relative to the medium, positive opposite wave propagation toward the source.
variables.domain: Finite -v<u_o<v in the declared subsonic observer application profile; zero stationary observer.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced signed u_o maps to +/- observer v_o; positive toward source.

variables.context: Same constant-frequency acoustic source and observer on one propagation line, homogeneous medium at rest in the stated frame, fixed medium composition/phase/temperature/pressure, and constant collinear subsonic endpoint velocities. Positive u_s is toward observer; positive u_o is toward source, so comoving endpoints have u_o=-u_s.
variables.definition: Positive rate of acoustic phase arrivals at the moving observer; frequency rather than frequency difference.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive on this branch; shift f_o-f_s may be positive, negative or zero.
